q: All of the following refer to the value of a color, except?
n: Value is how light or dark a color is, and it is also called lightness, brightness or luminance. Intensity (chroma or saturation) is a separate dimension: the purity or strength of the hue. Source: Munsell Color System (hue, value, chroma); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color).

q: Which of the following has the largest effect on vernacular architecture?
n: Vernacular buildings respond first to climate (sun, rain, wind, temperature) and to the locally available materials and ground conditions. Form, roof pitch, openings and construction follow from these. Source: Rapoport, House Form and Culture; Oliver, Encyclopedia of Vernacular Architecture of the World.

q: According to Charles Jencks, the death of modernism happened when the Pruitt-Igoe housing project was demolished in 1972. Who designed this housing project?
n: Minoru Yamasaki, later the architect of the World Trade Center, designed the Pruitt-Igoe housing project in St. Louis (1954). Charles Jencks dated the "death of modern architecture" to its demolition on 15 July 1972 at 3:32 p.m. Source: Jencks, The Language of Post-Modern Architecture (1977).

q: It refers to the scientific study of architecture.
n: Architectonics is the science or systematic study of architecture: the principles of design and construction, and the structural logic of a building. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Architectonics); Merriam-Webster.

q: Which architectural style or movement is a reaction against the industrial revolution?
n: The Arts and Crafts movement of William Morris and John Ruskin rejected the shoddy machine-made goods of the Industrial Revolution. It championed handcraft, honest materials and the dignity of the craftsman. Source: Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture (Arts and Crafts); Curtis, Modern Architecture Since 1900.

q: A common clause in a contract of service that binds the successors and permitted assigns of each party to the contract.
n: It is also known as the Binding Effect Clause. You can see in most, but not all, contract services, including Client-Architect Service Agreements. The "Successors and Assigns" clause binds each party, and the party's successors, legal representatives and permitted assigns, to the contract's obligations. It keeps the agreement enforceable if a party is replaced. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202 / Architect's Guidelines (Contract for Architectural Services – General Provisions).

q: What is required before presenting an architect’s previous works to the client?
n: An architect can present his portfolio or previous works to the client even without a service agreement. Showing a portfolio of previous works is part of marketing and selection. No agreement, downpayment or fee is needed before showing it, though the work must be presented truthfully. Source: UAP Code of Ethical Conduct (relations with prospective clients); Architect's Guidelines (2016), Selection of the Architect.

q: Three friends who just passed the board exam can form the following together, except?
n: A sole proprietorship, also known as individual entrepreneurship, or proprietorship, is a type of enterprise owned and run by one person. As opposed to a partnership and a corporation, a sole proprietorship has no legal personality distinct and separate between the owner and the business. A sole proprietorship has, by definition, only one owner. Three architects can instead form a partnership, a corporation or an architectural firm. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37 (practice through firms, partnerships, corporations); Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1767 (partnership).

q: Which of the following is considered a good basis for hiring a foreign architect?
n: A foreign architect may be engaged only where Filipino expertise is lacking, and an understudy or counterpart Filipino architect must be assigned for the transfer of technology and knowledge. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38 (Foreign Architects – Special Permit and Transfer of Technology).

q: Which of the following is an overhead cost?
n: Overhead costs are those that are not directly related to the production of goods or services but are necessary for the operation of a business. Examples of overhead costs include rent, utilities, insurance, legal fees, office supplies, advertising, payroll, and accounting fees. Overhead (indirect) costs keep the office running regardless of any single project, such as rent, utilities and administrative salaries. Materials and labor are direct project costs. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense; Halpin, Construction Management (overhead).

q: Which type of estimate is ideal for a client presentation?
n: A Bill of Quantities or BOQ is ideal when presenting to a client since it is more understandable for them. Take note of the difference between the bill of materials and the bill of quantities. A Bill of Quantities lists each work item with its quantity, unit cost and amount by trade. That is the clear, priced breakdown suited to presenting the probable cost to a client. A bill of materials lists only materials. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate; Architect's Guidelines (2016), Cost Estimates.

q: This is where the bidders can clarify some of the details of the project.
n: The pre-bid conference is held before bid submission. Prospective bidders ask questions and clarify the bidding documents, and any change is issued as a supplemental bid bulletin. Source: RA 9184 Revised IRR, Sec. 22 (Pre-bid Conference).

q: This is the first phase of architectural design.
n: Regular design services begin with the Schematic Design Phase, followed by Design Development and then Contract Documents. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202 / Architect's Guidelines (2016), Detailed Architectural Design Services phases.

q: Who secures the final occupancy permit?
n: Per the exam key, the contractor completes the turnover requirements, such as the construction logbook and as-built plans, that support the application for the certificate of occupancy. Code note: the NBC lets the owner/permittee file the application, assisted by the contractor and supervisor. Source: PD 1096 (NBCP), Sec. 309 (Certificate of Occupancy); 2004 Revised IRR, Rule III.

q: Who was the first PRC Outstanding Architect?
n: Otilio Arellano won the first PRC Outstanding Architect in 1977. Otilio A. Arellano, designer of the Philippine Pavilion at the 1964 New York World's Fair, received the first PRC Outstanding Professional award for architecture. Source: Professional Regulation Commission, Outstanding Professional of the Year awardees; CCP Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Architecture).

q: What is the minimum width of minor roads in an open market subdivision?
n: PD 957 standards require a minimum right-of-way of 8.00 m for minor roads in open-market subdivisions. Major roads require 10.00 m. Source: PD 957 (Subdivision and Condominium Buyers' Protective Decree) Revised IRR, Design Standards – Roads.

q: In what year was Batas Pambansa 220 approved and first promulgated?
n: BP 220 was approved in March 1982, and promulgated in June 1982. The Revised IRR was released in 2008. Batas Pambansa Blg. 220 was approved on 25 March 1982. It set the standards for economic and socialized housing. Source: BP 220 (1982) and its Revised IRR (HLURB, 2008).

q: What is the absolute minimum area of parks and playgrounds in an open market subdivision?
n: PD 957 requires parks and playgrounds of 3.5% to 9% of the gross area depending on density, and never less than 100 sqm. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR, Design Standards – Parks and Playgrounds.

q: What differentiates a pathwalk and an alley in an economic housing subdivision?
o: An alley can serve as property access
A pathwalk can be used as property access
A pathwalk cannot be used as property access
An alley is a private walkway
n: Take note of the difference between an alley and a pathwalk. An alley is only used as an emergency passageway and to break a block. It is not allowed to be used for property access. On the other hand, a pathwalk can be used as property access only in socialized housing. The width of alleys is 2m. minimum width of pathwalks is 3m, while the minimum. Under the BP 220 standards, a pathwalk (3.0 m) may serve as direct property access for socialized housing units. An alley (2.0 m) is only a pedestrian/emergency passage connecting two streets and is not a property access. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Sec. 2 (Definitions) and Design Standards – Circulation.

q: What is the minimum firewall thickness for socialized rowhouses?
n: BP 220 requires firewalls between socialized row houses to be masonry at least 150 mm (about 6 in) thick, with at least a one-hour fire rating. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Design Standards – Firewalls.

q: What method of compensation is ideal for a continuous series of projects?
n: For a continuing series of projects, compensating the architect with a professional fee plus reimbursable expenses keeps billing flexible as each project's scope varies. A retainer is the other common option. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.2.1.4 (Professional Fee plus Expenses) and 7.2.1.6 (Retainer).

q: What is the recommended minimum fee for a project manager?
n: Project management services are compensated at about 2% to 5% of the project construction cost, so the recommended minimum is 2%. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 9 – Construction/Project Management Services (fee 2% to 5% of PCC).

q: Who approves the fire safety documentary requirements?
n: The Bureau of Fire Protection reviews and approves the fire safety documents (the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance and the FSIC) before building and occupancy permits are issued. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (Enforcement, Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance).

q: A contractor's requests for payment can be made, at most, ____ every month.
n: Progress billings are made once a month. The contractor submits a monthly statement of work accomplished for the architect's certification of payment. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions of the Contract, Progress Payments); RA 9184 Revised IRR, Annex E.

q: Who orders the implementation of a project?
n: Only the owner, who funds the project, authorizes and orders its implementation. The architect and consultants advise and administer the contract on the owner's behalf. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Obligations of the Owner/Client.

q: This structure is a space with a roof supported by 134 gigantic papyrus columns.
n: The Great Hypostyle Hall is a large pillared-hall in the ancient Egyptian temple of Amun-Re, also known as the Karnak Temple. Great hypostyle hall was begun by Seti I, and completed by Ramesses II. The hall covers an area of 50,000 sq ft (5,000 sq meters) and filled with 134 gigantic stone columns with 12 larger columns standing 80 feet (24 m) high lining the central aisle. The Great Hypostyle Hall at Karnak, built under Seti I and Ramesses II, has 134 papyrus columns in 16 rows. The 12 central columns are about 21 m high. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture.

q: It is the first successful attempt to construct a straight faced pyramid.
n: But take note that it was not the first attempt since the Meidum Pyramid was also straight faced but it collapsed. Sneferu's Red Pyramid at Dahshur was the first successful true, smooth-sided pyramid. The Meidum attempt collapsed, and the Bent Pyramid changed angle midway. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Lehner, The Complete Pyramids.

q: Egyptian monumental pillars are called a/an
n: An obelisk is a tall, four-sided monolithic pillar that tapers to a pyramidion. It was usually set in pairs at temple entrances. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt).

q: Which is the predecessor of the pyramids?
n: The mastaba, a flat-roofed rectangular tomb with sloping sides, is the predecessor of the pyramid. Djoser's Step Pyramid began as stacked mastabas. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Lehner, The Complete Pyramids.

q: Which Giza pyramid has remaining casing on top?
n: Khafre's pyramid is the only Giza pyramid that still has part of its original Tura limestone casing near its apex. Source: Lehner, The Complete Pyramids; UNESCO World Heritage List – Memphis and its Necropolis.

q: Which theater was designed by the first National Artist for Architecture?
n: Juan Nakpil, the first National Artist for Architecture (1973), designed the Rizal Theater in Makati. The Metropolitan Theater is by Juan Arellano. Source: National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA), Order of National Artists – Juan F. Nakpil.

q: It is an example of thin shell construction inspired by the Space Age.
n: Leandro Locsin's Church of the Holy Sacrifice at UP Diliman (1955) has a thin-shell concrete dome. It was the first circular chapel in the Philippines with a central altar. Source: NCCA, National Artists – Leandro V. Locsin; National Historical Commission marker.

q: He represented Philippine architecture during the 1964 New York World's Fair and is the son of one of the first practicing Filipino architects in the 20th century.
n: Otilio Arellano designed the Philippine Pavilion at the 1964–65 New York World's Fair. He was the son of Arcadio Arellano, one of the first practicing Filipino architects of the 20th century. Source: Cultural Center of the Philippines Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Architecture).

q: Known as the Dean of the Filipino Architects.
n: Juan F. Nakpil, National Artist for Architecture, is called the Dean of Filipino Architects. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists – Juan F. Nakpil.

q: Who was the LIKHA Gold Medal Awardee in 2022?
n: Architect Jose Siao Ling received the UAP's LIKHA Gold Medal of Excellence in 2022, the association's highest award for an architect's body of work. Source: United Architects of the Philippines, National Convention awards (2022).

q: If conflicts arise between the contents of the construction drawings and specifications, which shall govern?
n: The general conditions provide that where the drawings and specifications conflict, the specifications govern, and written figures govern over scaled dimensions. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions of the Contract), Contract Documents – order of precedence.

q: Who provides the shop drawings?
n: Shop drawings are prepared by the contractor, subcontractor or fabricator to show how work will be fabricated and installed. The architect reviews them. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions), Shop Drawings; Architect's Guidelines (2016).

q: Who provides the detailed drawings?
n: While architects and engineers can be correct, designers is the more correct answer since it was not specified which type of detailed drawing is required. Detailed drawings come from the designers of each discipline: the architect for architectural details, engineers for theirs. Since the stem names no discipline, "designers" is the broadest correct answer. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Contract Documents Phase; RA 9266, Sec. 3 (Scope of Practice).

q: Which of the following is required for the release of a certificate of occupancy?
n: The sanitary permit and clearance under the Code on Sanitation are among the documents required before a certificate of occupancy is issued. Source: PD 856 (Code on Sanitation of the Philippines), Ch. XVIII and its IRR; PD 1096 (NBCP), Sec. 309.

q: Which law protects the owners of architectural documents from copyright infringement?
n: RA 8293, the Intellectual Property Code, protects architectural plans, drawings and works as copyrighted works against infringement. RA 9266, Sec. 20 also recognizes the architect's ownership of plans. Source: RA 8293, Sec. 172; RA 9266, Sec. 20.

q: An architect is hired to design the architectural interiors of a new hotel. How much should be the minimum professional fee if the architectural interior project costs Php 10 million?
n: For this type of service, the recommended professional fee is 10% to 15%. We will use 10% since it mentioned the minimum. Php 10,000,000 x 0.1 = Php 1,000,000. For Architectural Interiors, the recommended professional fee is 10% to 15% of the cost of work. The minimum on a ₱10 million interior project is 10%, or ₱1.0 million. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.1.

q: Using the same data in number 41, how much should the architect receive after providing the preliminary design?
n: For architectural interiors, 30% of the fee is paid upon submission of the preliminary design: 30% × ₱1,000,000 = ₱300,000. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.2 (Manner of Payment).

q: Using the same data in number 41, how much should the architect receive after submitting the final designs?
n: Upon submission of the final design, the architect receives a further 50% of the fee: 50% × ₱1,000,000 = ₱500,000. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.2 (Manner of Payment).

q: Using the same data in number 41, how much should the architect receive after the completion of the project?
n: The remaining 20% of the fee (₱200,000) is paid in proportion to construction progress, so it is fully received upon completion. 30% + 50% + 20% = 100% of ₱1,000,000. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.2.

q: What is the recommended minimum professional fee for architectural acoustics?
n: Acoustic design shares the architectural interiors fee range of 10% to 15% of the cost of work, so the minimum is 10%. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.1 (AI, Acoustic Design, Lighting and Site Development Planning).

q: What is the minimum professional fee that an architect can receive for regular design services if the project is a city library? Assume that a single contract between the architect and the owner is preferred while the architect has contracts with allied professionals.
n: In this question, it can be derived that the service means Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS). And since a city library is under Group 2 structures (moderate complexity). Therefore, the answer is 6% of the PCC. A library is a Group 2 building. With one contract covering architecture and the allied engineering consultants (DAEDS), the fee for a project of ₱50 million and below is 6% of the project cost. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2, DAEDS table).

q: A government building is to be constructed in Metro Manila in 3 years. Before the project proceeds, numerous conferences are conducted to tackle different aspects of the project's feasibility. You were invited to be part of one of its conferences as an architect who has a wide knowledge of underground architecture. Which of the following can be an appropriate way to compensate for your service?
n: For these types of cases, where a day of service is only required from the architect (i.e. attending meetings, conferences, etc.), per diem/honorarium is the most appropriate. Page iz of i3. One-time attendance at conferences as a consultant is best compensated per diem. The client pays a fixed daily rate (plus expenses) for each day of service, since no design documents are produced. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.2.1.7 (Per Diem, Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses).

q: The first professional organization for architects in the Philippines is an organization for architects and:
n: The first organization of architects and its allied professionals is the Academia de Arquitectura y Aguimensura de Filipinos and later renamed Academia de Inginieria, Arquitectura y Agrimensura de Filipinas (AIAAF). The first professional organization of Filipino architects was the Academia de Arquitectura y Agrimensura de Filipinas, for architects and land surveyors. It was later renamed to include engineers. Source: Philippine architectural history references (CCP Encyclopedia of Philippine Art); UAP history.

q: What is the recommended minimum professional fee for an architect providing DADS for a residential condominium project?
n: Take note that even though the project is residential, it is a condominium so it is considered under the Group 2 project classification with MODERATE COMPLEXITY. A residential condominium is Group 2. Its DADS fee (architectural design only) is 60% of the 6% DAEDS rate, which is 3.6% of the project cost. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2, DADS table).

q: What is the standard height of handrails in an accessible ramp?
n: BP 344 requires handrails on both sides of ramps, at 0.70 m and 0.90 m above the ramp surface. That serves both wheelchair users and ambulant people. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, Minimum Requirements – Handrails; BP 344 2024 Revised IRR.
